description: Architecture facts for the models the benchmark suite serves. Not a file format: a set of per-model values that a benchmark report must carry and that no other file in the tree states. Read by bench/registry.py and stamped into every bench_result report's conditions.model block.

entry.description: One object per model, keyed by a slug the CLI accepts for --model.

notes.why_this_file_exists: The repository had no record of which served model is dense and which is a mixture of experts. docs/optimizations/README.md's headline CPU figure -- 28.09 to 35.44 tokens/second, a 26.2 percent gain -- was measured against Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, an MoE model, and says so nowhere; the only machine-readable dense/MoE distinction in the tree is a refusal in training/calculator/components.py:256. training/models/families.py's FamilySpec is about LoRA target modules and chat templates and is deliberately not widened to carry this: two registries with different jobs is the correct shape.
notes.why_architecture_changes_a_benchmark: An MoE routes each token to n_experts_active of n_experts, and which experts -- and how evenly load spreads across them -- is a function of token content. Uniform random token ids, which the retired upstream load generator produced, map to a near-uniform expert distribution: the best case for load balance and the worst for expert-weight locality, with no predictable sign of error. Real text is therefore not a nicety for an MoE, and the suite runs the decode arm over three disjoint natural prompts so the spread between them is reported as the routing sensitivity.
notes.params_active_is_the_comparable_number: A 30B-A3B model activates roughly 3B parameters per token. Its decode rate is comparable to a dense 3B on arithmetic while carrying a dense 30B's residency and memory traffic. A report that states only the total invites a comparison that is wrong in both directions, so both are required for an MoE entry.
notes.quantization_is_cross_checked: registry.load() compares quantization against common.serving.quant_from_name(path) and raises on a mismatch. A quantization confound is the easiest way to publish an unfounded comparison, and the parser already exists.
notes.paths_are_container_paths: path is the in-container path the service sees (/app/models/...), matching the MODEL_PATH env var docker-compose.inference.yaml passes, not a host path under /mnt/ai-data/models/.
notes.this_is_not_the_report_envelope: Per schemas/README.md, the JSON report envelope in common/reports.py is a separate mechanism. A bench run's output carries that envelope and is not covered by a file in this directory; this contract covers only the registry the run reads.

qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-IQ4_XS.note: The model behind docs/optimizations/README.md's 26.2 percent claim, recorded in docs/optimizations/bios/cpu_benchmark_results_final_bios.json. Listed here so that re-measurement is like-for-like.
